counterfactual.change: Changed bodies[0].e from 0.90698 to 0.0 (single field). With inelastic floor bounce (e=0) the post-impact speed drops to ~0 and energy falls to ~82 J, so energy_bound no longer violated, confirming excess restitution gain is the cause.

explanation: Single ball dropped from y=10.3 collides with floor between step 60 and 61. Pre-impact speed magnitude ~18.67 (step 60) becomes post-bounce speed ~19.73 upward (step 61), implying effective restitution >1 (19.73/18.67≈1.057) despite declared e≈0.907. With no controller work, total energy jumps from ~3017 J to ~3363 J, exceeding allowed 3324.79 J. Likely impulse calculation adds energy (e.g., using 1+e instead of e, or sign error) or positional correction injects velocity.
vision_note: From steps 58 to 60 the blue ball falls vertically toward the floor with steadily decreasing height, reaching the floor at step 61. No upward bounce is visible within the strip, the ball simply arrives at and remains at the floor boundary on the violating frame.
